The textbook transmission-line design - a half guide wavelength less Hammerstad's fringing extension at each open edge - kept because the worked examples are written in it. Full-wave it resonates 0.5-7% below f0 (full_wave_resonance_hz). The patch to build is L.

Fitted as a ratio to L_textbook over eps_r 1-12, h/lambda0 0.003-0.05 and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 <= 0.1 (0.21% worst, 0.12% held out); exactly L_textbook on a vanishingly thin board, NaN past h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 = 0.1. the transmission-line model's effective (radiating-slot) length, on the textbook design it belongs to

analysis.notes: Where the TEXTBOOK length L_textbook would resonate, full-wave (L itself resonates at f0): otahub.num.patch_sdm, the spectral-domain method of moments (edge-exact currents in both directions, exact slab Green's function), which an FDTD ringdown of the same patch (otahub.num.patch_fdtd, taken to zero cell size) matches to 0.013% in frequency and 0.2% in Q on two boards. Fitted as the ratio to f0 over eps_r 1-12, h/lambda0 0.003-0.05, h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 <= 0.1 (0.20% worst on 68 full-wave solutions, 0.13% on 8 held out), with no constant term, so it is exactly f0 on a vanishingly thin board. The transmission-line design with Hammerstad's fringing extension lands 0.5-1% LOW on the thinnest boards, 2.2-2.8% low at h = 0.01 lambda0 and up to 7% low on thick high-permittivity board - not the '1-3%' this spec's validity used to allow. NaN past h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 = 0.1.
surface-wave loss becomes significant above about 0.02 on high-permittivity substrates

Radiation Q of the patch resonant at f0, FULL-WAVE: otahub.num.patch_sdm, the spectral-domain method of moments (edge-exact currents in both directions, exact slab Green's function), which an FDTD ringdown of the same patch (otahub.num.patch_fdtd, taken to zero cell size) matches to 0.013% in frequency and 0.2% in Q on two boards. Fitted as ln(Q (h/lambda0) c1/eps_r) in 1/eps_r and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 over eps_r 1-12, h/lambda0 0.003-0.05, h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 <= 0.1 (0.91% worst on 68 full-wave solutions, 0.37% on 8 held out). The cavity current radiated through the slab (otahub.num.patch_q), which this spec used, runs 1.6-28% HIGH - least on thin board, most on thick - so every bandwidth it gave was that much too narrow. Surface waves are not in this Q; see surface_wave_efficiency.

Broadside directivity of the cavity mode on a vanishingly thin board, where the patch current radiated through the slab and the magnetic currents on ALL the patch's walls are the same field. Solved by otahub.num.patch_q and fitted as 3 + a series in 1/sqrt(eps_r) (0.074%), so it goes to exactly 3 - a horizontal magnetic dipole over ground - as the patch shrinks. It is 2-10% above the two-slot formula: the fields along the non-radiating edges cancel in the principal planes but not in the total power.

The substrate's own effect on the space wave, as the ratio of otahub.num.patch_q's directivity - the cavity current radiated through the grounded slab - to the thin-substrate value, fitted in 1/eps_r and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 with no constant term, so it is exactly 1 on a vanishingly thin board: 0.18% worst on 154 solved designs, 0.13% on 10 held out, over eps_r 1-12, h/lambda0 0.003-0.05 and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 <= 0.1. It spans 0.99 to 1.22 there - it matters most on electrically thick high-permittivity board.

SOLVED: the thin-substrate directivity times the substrate factor; NaN past h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 = 0.1, where the cavity model stops. Checked full-wave: otahub.num.patch_sdm, a spectral-domain method of moments that solves for the patch current instead of assuming it, puts the rectangular patch's broadside directivity within 0.3-0.9%% of this on air, eps_r 2.2, FR-4 and eps_r 10.2. It replaces the two-slot formula 2 D1/(1 + G12/G1), which was 7.5% low on eps_r 2.2 and FR-4, 10% on air and 13% on eps_r 10.2 against the full-wave solution: it left out the non-radiating edges and the substrate. At the full-wave-resonant design the full-wave directivity is within 0.02-2.5% of this, the largest difference on thick air board.
VSWR-2 bandwidth from the full-wave radiation Q: radiation only, lossless, surface waves not counted (fractional_bandwidth_vswr2_with_surface_waves counts them).

Space-wave power over space plus surface-wave power, full-wave, for the patch resonant at f0 (0.11% worst on 68 full-wave solutions, 0.13% on 8 held out). It agrees with Jackson and Alexopoulos's thin-substrate closed form for a horizontal dipole to 0.0-0.5% on thin board, and falls below it as the board thickens - 7.5% below at eps_r 10.2, h = 0.03 lambda0. Exactly 1 on air; 0.66 at eps_r 6, h = 0.04 lambda0. Capped at 1, which the fit would otherwise overshoot on air by a few parts in 10^4.
VSWR-2 bandwidth with the surface wave counted as the loss it is to the feed: the total Q is the radiation Q times the surface-wave efficiency. Still no dielectric or conductor loss.

Balanis 14-12 in its EXACT closed form: G1 = I1/(120*pi^2) with I1 = -2 + cos(X) + X*Si(X) + sin(X)/X and X = k0*W. This replaces the (1/90)*(W/lambda0)^2 small-width branch, which runs 10% high on the Balanis Example 14.1 patch (1.7389e-3 against the exact 1.5748e-3). Verified against numerical quadrature of the integral to eight figures.

Mutual-to-self slot conductance ratio. The exact quantity is the integral of Balanis 14-18a divided by 14-12, which has no closed form, so this is a polynomial fitted to that integral over the whole practical design space: k0*L from 0.8 to 3.3 and k0*W from 1.15 to 3.25, which is what eps_r between 1 and 12 produces. Worst error 0.0021 in the ratio, and under 0.1% in the resulting resistance. The older approximation G12 = G1*J0(k0*L) is the leading term of this and is 28% low, because the weighting favours theta near 90 degrees but not nearly as strongly as that form assumes. Evaluated on the textbook length: the edge resistance is the transmission-line model's, and the model's own slot spacing is what it was derived for.
Balanis 14-17 with the PLUS sign, which is the one the dominant TM010 mode takes. Neglecting G12 entirely overestimates Rin by about 25%, so it cannot be dropped.

Inverts Rin(y0) = Rin0*cos^2(pi*y0/L) (Balanis 14-20). The cos^2 law degrades for deep insets and wide notches; verify in a solver. The inset FRACTION y0/L comes from the transmission-line model; the depth is that fraction of the full-wave length L, the patch actually built.

archetypes.name: Circular microstrip patch
archetypes.summary: Circular microstrip patch in the TM110 mode, with the directivity integrated from the cavity-model fields rather than assumed.

parameters.name: physical radius
parameters.description: the radius to build, FDTD-corrected (see radius_factor)

parameters.name: probe radius / effective radius
parameters.description: where the probe sits, as a fraction of a_e

synthesis.notes: Balanis 14-65, rewritten in SI. The published constant 8.791e9 yields centimetres; 8.791e7 yields metres, which is what the rest of this toolkit speaks. F is the radius before the fringing correction.
Balanis 14-64. The bracket depends only on the ratio h/F, so the formula is unit-agnostic and works directly in metres - the previous version carried factors of 100 to work in centimetres instead.

SOLVED by FDTD (otahub.num.patch_fdtd.circular_ringdown: the outline staircased onto the grid, the slab infinite): the factor that brings the cavity-model radius to resonance at f0. Fitted over eps_r 2.2-10.2 and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 0.065-0.095 on boards solved at three to five cell sizes and extrapolated to zero (1.1% worst), made to vanish as the board thins; held out, eps_r 3.0 and 6.15 land within 0.3%. A staircased curve or slant converges unevenly, so read it as about 1% good. NaN past h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 = 0.1.

The radius to build: the cavity model's times the FDTD factor. Built to the cavity radius alone the patch resonates 2-7% LOW on the boards surveyed - the fringing correction (Balanis 14-64) holds within about 1% on thin board and falls short as the board thickens. Built to this radius, the held-out boards resonate at 0.993 f0 (eps_r 3, 0.05), 0.990 f0 (eps_r 6.15, 0.08).
Balanis 14-66, the fringing-corrected radius the fields actually see
The one number the pattern depends on. At resonance k*a_e = 1.8412 with k = k0*sqrt(eps_r), so k0*a_e = 1.8412/sqrt(eps_r) and the directivity is a function of permittivity alone.

analysis.notes: forward check from the cavity model's effective radius: returns f0 to within the 0.3% by which Balanis's radius formula (14-64) inverts his resonance (14-66). It checks the cavity model, not the built radius a, which the FDTD factor has moved.

THIN-SUBSTRATE value, from the TM110 fields' J0 -/+ J2 edge currents radiating in free space over the ground - exact on a vanishingly thin board, where it and the patch current radiated through the slab are the same field. Integrated from the TM110 far fields (Balanis 14-79/14-80), whose angular dependence is J0 -/+ J2 of k0*a_e*sin(theta), over the UPPER hemisphere only - the ground plane takes the rest. Fitted to that quadrature over k0*a_e in [0.45, 1.90], which is eps_r from 1 to 17; worst error 0.19%. This spec previously carried a hard-coded 6.3, which is 54% high on FR-4 and 84% high on eps_r = 10.2 - the very substrates a circular patch is chosen for.

The substrate's own effect on the space wave, as the ratio of otahub.num.patch_q's directivity - the cavity current radiated through the grounded slab - to the thin-substrate value, fitted in 1/eps_r and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 with no constant term, so it is exactly 1 on a vanishingly thin board: 0.23% worst on 154 solved designs, 0.07% on 10 held out, over eps_r 1-12, h/lambda0 0.003-0.05 and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 <= 0.1. It spans 0.97 to 1.22 there - it matters most on electrically thick high-permittivity board.

SOLVED: the thin-substrate directivity times the substrate factor, which the free-space edge-current model this spec used alone leaves out - it read up to 18% low on electrically thick board. NaN past h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 = 0.1. The same model, full-wave checked on the rectangular patch to 0.3-0.9%.
the free-space pattern integral itself (thin substrate), exposed because the radiation conductance is the same integral scaled

DERIVED HERE, NOT CHECKED AGAINST A PUBLISHED EXAMPLE. G = 2*P_rad/|V0|^2 from the same cavity-model fields as the directivity, which IS checked. The derivation is sound but the absolute level rests on the cavity model's edge-voltage normalisation, so treat the resistance below as a starting point to tune rather than a prediction. It is the free-space edge model's, like the thin-substrate directivity it shares its integral with; the substrate's effect on the radiated power (see substrate_directivity_factor) is NOT carried into it, so treat the edge and feed resistances as thin-substrate values.
at rho0 = a_e, where J1 peaks and the resistance is highest
R(rho0)/R_edge = [J1(k*rho0)/J1(k*a_e)]^2. Since k*a_e = 1.8412 at resonance for every substrate, this depends ONLY on rho0/a_e - the permittivity cancels out entirely, which is the useful part.

NaN when rho_frac a_eff lies past the built radius a: rho_frac is measured on the fringing-corrected radius, so near 1 the probe would stand off the copper (0.31 mm off at rho_frac 0.9 on the Balanis board). feed_resistance_ratio stays defined there, as the cos-law normalisation it is.

Q = omega W / P from otahub.num.patch_q: the cavity mode's stored energy against the space wave of the patch's own surface current on its grounded substrate (the transverse-equivalent-network slab factors - no surface waves, no loss). Fitted as ln(Q (h/lambda0) c1/eps_r) in 1/eps_r and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0, with Jackson's c1 = 1 - 1/eps_r + 0.4/eps_r^2 carrying the thin-substrate law, over 1 <= eps_r <= 12, 0.003 <= h/lambda0 <= 0.05 and h*sqrt(eps_r)/lambda0 <= 0.1: 0.49% worst on 201 solved designs, 0.24% on 10 held out. The arbiter reproduces Jackson's c1 to 0.02% for a vanishing patch on a thin substrate, and on air its broadside directivity matches the cavity model's edge-current integrals to 0.06%. NOT checked full-wave: for the rectangular patch the full-wave radiation Q is 1.6-22% below this same cavity-current model (least on thin board, most on thick), so treat this Q as an upper bound on thicker board and the bandwidth as a lower bound. The FDTD of this shape (patch_fdtd, on the boards that fixed its size) rings down with a TOTAL Q of 0.73-0.90 of this, falling with thickness and permittivity. Part of that gap is surface-wave power, which this radiation Q leaves out; how much is not separated here, so this Q stays the cavity model's.

NaN when rho_frac a_eff lies past the built radius a: rho_frac is measured on the fringing-corrected radius, so near 1 the probe would stand off the copper (0.31 mm off at rho_frac 0.9 on the Balanis board). feed_resistance_ratio stays defined there, as the cos-law normalisation it is.

VSWR-2 bandwidth from this shape's own solved radiation Q. It used the rectangular patch's simplified formula, which by luck lands within 13% for eps_r 2-12 but gives an air disc zero bandwidth and reads 27-51% low at eps_r 1.25-1.5.

broadside is the pattern peak throughout that range, checked; it would not be for a much larger k0*a_e

A half-space FDTD of the plate on air (otahub.num.patch_fdtd.shorted_ringdown, taken to zero cell size) puts two quite different plates - h = 0.036 lambda with W = 0.12 lambda, and h = 0.02 lambda with W = 0.2 lambda - at L + h = 0.2428 and 0.2423 wavelengths of their own resonance: the lambda/4 rule builds a plate that resonates 3% low. The spectral MoM (otahub.num.patch_sdm) puts the unshorted plate of twice the length 6.7% and 3.1% higher than the FDTD's shorted one - the shorting wall's inductance, as for the shorted patch on a substrate. Two designs, so the constant is a calibration, not a law. A NARROWER strip at one corner lengthens the current path: L + h + strip_phi W = 0.2425 lambda, strip_phi growing as ln(W/Ws). From a survey with the whole-plate FDTD (otahub.num.patch_fdtd.pifa_ringdown): 21 plates (h 0.014-0.065, W 0.054-0.22 wavelengths, W/L up to 1.5), each with a full-width short and corner strips of 1/2 to 1/30 of its width, 70 designs; every strip run's frequency is corrected by its own plate's full-width run against the 0.2425 calibration. The survey's 3-4 cells across h cannot confirm that beyond a few percent: on the one plate run at two grids, refining moves the full-width resonance up 2.5% and a W/6 strip's down 0.8% (both extrapolated), opposite ways, so the ratio the law rests on is itself uncertain by about 3% there. The dominant Neumann eigenfunction of the equilateral triangle was found, not quoted: the six plane waves of magnitude k = 4*pi/(3*a) that live on the hexagonal star span a 2-D null space of the magnetic-wall condition, and the member symmetric about a median is the one a feed on that median excites. All THREE walls then radiate, as magnetic line currents M = 2*Ez*(z_hat x n_hat); each wall integral is exact in closed form because Ez restricted to a straight side is a sum of twelve exponentials. Only the hemisphere integral is numerical, and it converges to nine digits. The fit variable is k0*a_eff, which the synthesis pins to exactly 4*pi/(3*sqrt(eps_r)) whatever the substrate height, so D depends on eps_r ALONE. The form is D = 3 + (k0*a_eff)^2*g(k0*a_eff), which is right in the small-patch limit by construction rather than by luck: a vanishing patch is a horizontal magnetic dipole over a ground plane, D = 3 exactly, and the raw integral returns 3.0000039 at k0*a_eff = 0.0042. archetypes.notes: TWO MODES, ONE FEED. Cutting two opposite corners of a square splits its degenerate pair into two DIAGONAL modes: the one polarised along the cut diagonal rises in frequency, the other barely moves. Fed so that both are excited equally, each resonance contributes +-45 degrees of phase at the frequency midway between them, which is circular polarisation. Everything below was checked against a finite-element cavity model of the actual truncated outline (otahub/num/patch_cavity.py: Neumann modes on linear triangles, a probe feed, one loss Q for every mode, the broadside polarisation summed over 30 modes), converged to 0.004% between 240 and 480 cells per side. THE SPLIT is f0/Q, not f0/(2Q) as this spec used to say: 90 degrees at equal amplitude needs the modes at f0(1 -+ 1/(2Q)), so f0/(2Q) is each mode's offset from the centre, not their separation. The cavity model gives perfect CP at Q = 1/split to within 0.5%. THE FEED goes on a CENTRELINE of the square - the line through the midpoints of two opposite sides - not on a diagonal. On either diagonal one of the two modes is identically zero, so a diagonal feed excites one mode and radiates linear polarisation (the cavity model gives an axial ratio of about 3000 dB there). The diagonal feed belongs to the NEARLY-SQUARE patch, whose modes lie along the sides. THE CUT. First-order perturbation gives split = 2 dS/S, hence the classic dS/S = 1/(2Q); the finite-element split falls below 2 dS/S as the cut grows (1.97 at c/L = 0.06, 1.93 at 0.14), so the classic cut is 0.2% short in c at Q = 1150 and 2.6% short at Q = 12. The cut here is the solved one. THE SQUARE. The CP centre sits ABOVE the uncut square's resonance, by 0.5/Q at small cuts and 0.39/Q at Q = 12, because only one mode moves. This spec used to size the square to resonate AT f0, which put the CP centre 0.79% high in its own 2.4 GHz case - outside the +-0.29% axial-ratio band, leaving 7.9 dB of axial ratio at f0. The square is now sized for f_sq, below f0 by exactly that offset. BANDWIDTHS from the same two-mode picture, both confirmed by the cavity model to 4 digits: the 3 dB axial-ratio band is 0.347107/Q and the VSWR-2 band is sqrt(2)/Q - TWICE a single mode's, because the two staggered resonances flatten the impedance. At the CP centre the two-mode impedance is exactly real.

parameters.description: parasitic length over driven length (widths scale alike); synthesised so the parasitic is the survey's best 0.36-0.375 wavelengths less 0.005 - 1.145 on the default board. A denser driven layer, whose patch is shorter, wants a larger ratio; give it to override

synthesis.notes: The textbook transmission-line length of the driven patch alone.

The driven patch's length that resonates at f0 ON ITS OWN, full-wave (the rectangular patch's correction: otahub.num.patch_sdm, FDTD-checked), 2.8% shorter than the textbook one on 1.6 mm eps_r 2.2 at 2.4 GHz. The parasitic above it moves the stack's modes, which this does not model.

INDICATIVE. The air gap that gives the widest band, moved 0.005 wavelengths up from it. Solved by the two-layer spectral MoM with a probe (otahub.num.stacked) on 20 driven boards - eps_r 2.2-10.2, h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda 0.0185-0.0385, 16 fitted and 4 held out (tests/data/stacked_patch_rules.json) - the best gap is 0.0675-0.085 wavelengths, fitted to 0.003. It sits at a cliff: 0.005 less gap leaves under a third of the band on 18 of the 20 boards, while 0.005 more keeps 83-97%. So the rule errs toward more gap; with the parasitic below it keeps 91-99% of the best band (95-98% held out). Outside the surveyed boards the board's variables are held at the survey's edge. Supply h2_over_lambda to override.

INDICATIVE. The parasitic's length, as a ratio to the driven patch: the length that gives the widest band, 0.36-0.375 wavelengths on every surveyed board and fitted to 0.004, shortened 0.005 wavelengths with the gap's move (same survey). As a ratio it runs from 1.15 on eps_r 2.2 to 2.4 on 10.2, since the driven patch shrinks with the board's permittivity and the parasitic, in air, does not. Supply size_ratio to override.

The parasitic's length. Solved by the two-layer spectral MoM (otahub.num.patch_sdm.StackedPatch) and checked by FDTD: the stack this spec used to default to (a 0.03-wavelength air gap, ratio 0.95) has its two coupled modes at 0.993 and 1.378 f0 (FDTD at 2-8 cells across the driven layer, extrapolated; the MoM's poles 0.993 and 1.375) - the upper one far out of any band, and 1.5% of VSWR-2 band about f0. Its characteristic-mode zero sits at 1.393: for a mode of Q 13 that is 1.2% above the natural frequency, which is why a coarse FDTD once seemed to disagree. At a 0.09 gap and a ratio of 1.1 the stack is double-tuned - resistance peaks at 0.99 and 1.06 f0 - and the band is 11.5% about f0, 12.4% at its own centre; the FDTD of that design with a single probe gives 12.5% against the MoM's 12.3%. The note here once said the parasitic, being in a lower permittivity, is made smaller: the wrong way round, as a patch in air needs a longer length.

INDICATIVE. The probe, on the centre line, 0.9 of the driven patch's half length from its centre: the best feed was 0.84-0.95 of it on every board and design surveyed that double-tuned, and the band moves little across that range. The design's own best position comes from `otahub stack`.

analysis.notes: the driven patch on its own, the textbook formula; the best stack on the board reaches about 8.4 times it (best_stack_bandwidth_vswr2)

The honest cost: the best stacks surveyed stand 0.08-0.10 wavelengths tall, six to eight times the driven layer. Height alone does not buy the band - the 0.043-wavelength stack this spec used to default to, not double-tuned, has 1.5%; tuning the pair does.

INDICATIVE, and not this design's own band: the widest VSWR-2 band about f0 that the best air gap and parasitic reach on this driven board, probe-fed with a series element tuned for the band (its own reactance not solved). Solved by the two-layer spectral MoM with a probe over gap (0.0025-wavelength steps) and parasitic length (0.005) on 20 boards, eps_r 2.2-10.2 and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda 0.0185-0.0385; fitted in ln(band) to 4.1%, 2.5% on 4 boards held out. 8.2 to 21 times the single patch's band, more on higher permittivity: the 8.4 this spec used came from four boards searched more coarsely, whose bests sat at the cliff's lip and came out 1-18% short. The design this spec builds (the rules for h2_over_lambda and size_ratio) reaches 91-99% of it. NaN outside the surveyed boards or with a dielectric gap. The gate takes the survey's edge boards with rounding room: h = t lambda/sqrt(eps_r) at t = 0.0185 computed back to 0.018499999999999996 and the edge board itself read NaN. One board (eps_r 3, t 0.0185) has a three-way tie for its best band (0.110 at gap/parasitic 0.08/0.365, 0.0825/0.36 and 0.0825/0.365); the fits take the stored first.

SOLVED: broadside directivity at f0 of the currents the probe drives on both patches (the two-layer spectral MoM, its far field balancing its own reaction to 1e-14). It follows the parasitic's size and hardly the board or the feed: 8.0 dBi for the stack this spec used to default to, 9.06 at the 0.09-gap, 1.1-ratio default that followed, 9.23 at the design the rules now build on that board, 8.7-9.4 over parasitics 0.33-0.37 wavelengths long. Fitted in the parasitic's length and width and the gap over 44 designs on three boards (0.09 dB worst); a fourth board held out, 0.07 dB. NaN for a dielectric gap or outside the designs solved. It replaces a 7.5 (8.75 dBi) placeholder. At each surveyed board's best design the solved directivity is 9.16-9.41 dBi for eps_r 2.2-10.2; inside this fit's eps_r 2.2-4.4 it matches them to 0.015 dB, beyond it reads 0.04-0.13 dB low, so its domain stays at 4.4.

validity: the design's own band is not in this spec: best_stack_bandwidth_vswr2 is what the best gap and parasitic achieve on the board (indicative, a fit over twenty solved boards), and `otahub stack` solves the design as given
gap and size ratio interact strongly: on the default board the old 0.09 and 1.1 give 11.5% about f0, a ratio of 1.2 gives no band at f0, and the 0.03 and 0.95 this spec used to default to give 1.5%

solved for an air gap (eps_r2 = 1) over driven layers of h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda 0.0185-0.0385: the band and the gap and parasitic rules over eps_r 2.2-10.2, the directivity over eps_r 2.2-4.4; a dielectric gap is not solved here
the probe's own reactance is not solved (the FDTD puts it near 13-14 ohm on the default board, the parallel-plate formula at 27); the bands assume a series capacitor tuned for it
L is the driven patch's full-wave length on its own; the parasitic moves the stack's two modes, which the two-layer spectral MoM solves (checked by FDTD to 0.2% on both)

the air gap and parasitic the spec builds (h2_over_lambda, size_ratio) are fitted to the best band on driven boards eps_r 2.2-10.2 and h sqrt(eps_r)/lambda 0.0185-0.0385, then moved 0.005 wavelengths from the cliff at the best; outside those boards they hold the survey's edge values. Err toward more gap when building: less gap loses the band fast

known_cases.source: Geometry only, which is the part of this archetype that is actually derived: a 0.03-wavelength gap at 2.4 GHz is 3.75 mm, making the stack 0.043 wavelengths tall in all.
The parasitic at 0.95 of the driven patch's full-wave length, 40.1478 mm - solved directly by otahub.num.patch_sdm for the patch alone (textbook 41.3192 mm).
otahub.num.patch_sdm solved directly for the driven patch alone: 40.1478 mm resonates at f0; the textbook 41.3192 mm does not.

The two-layer spectral MoM solved directly at the default stack (gap 0.09 wavelengths, ratio 1.1), a probe of 0.65 mm at 0.84 of the half length driving it at f0: broadside directivity of both patches' currents (the fit, not used here, gives it to 0.1 dB). (The design this spec defaulted to then: gap 0.09 wavelengths, size ratio 1.1.)

Two-layer spectral MoM with a probe (otahub.num.stacked) on this board (fit): the widest VSWR-2 band, 0.159, is reached at a gap of 0.08 and a parasitic 0.365 wavelengths long, solved over gap and length (tests/data/stacked_patch_rules.json). The rule builds that design moved 0.005 wavelengths from the cliff (gap up, parasitic shorter), so h2 and L2 here are the solved best so moved - not the fit's own output.

The rule builds that design moved 0.005 wavelengths from the cliff (gap up, parasitic shorter), so h2 and L2 here are the solved best so moved - not the fit's own output.
